title: Keto Chicken Bacon Ranch Casserole
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot), grams derived FROM the printed measure via db\densities.json (or the flagged USDA/label unit weights where densities has no row) so the two agree by construction; quantities quantized to house quarters, drift from the exact 4.6667x scale noted per line where it exceeds 5%.

ingredients.source_raw: 8 ounces cooked chicken breast shredded or diced (about 2 cups)
ingredients.notes: grams are RAW purchase weight matching the raw DB row: source 8 oz COOKED x 4.6667 = 37.3 oz cooked; at the DB's own 3 oz cooked = 4 oz raw factor that is 1411 g raw, quantized to 3 lb = 1361 g (-3.6%). Printed 3 lb and grams agree exactly. Cooked yield ~1021 g = ~7 cups at 140 g/cup (densities). NOT a florentine-class each-weight assumption: the source states a weight, and its own published macros validate the portion (see macro_cross_check). Board 6 of 7 stores, cheapest Baker's $1.99/lb.
exact scale 4.67 tbsp, quantized 4.75 tbsp (+1.8%) = 66.5 g at densities 14 g/tbsp, rounded 67. Salted and unsalted sit in the same commodity price class (florentine precedent). Board 7 of 7.

FRESH raw cauliflower to the fresh cauliflower commodity (unit each, per-head pricing, 4 of 7 stores, cheapest Fareway $1.98/each); the frozen-cauliflower-florets id would be a form-flip and was not used. NEW food-DB row added (USDA raw, 25 cal/100 g). densities.json has NO Cauliflower row (FLAGGED); grams from USDA 1 cup chopped = 107 g, 9.25 cups = 990 g (-0.9% vs exact 9.33 cups).

FULL-FAT cream cheese; deliberately NOT the existing 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese item (different product, different macros - mapping to it would deflate calories on a card with a calorie floor). cream-cheese commodity 7 of 7 stores, cheapest Sam's $0.1381/oz. NEW food-DB row added (USDA generic, 350 cal/100 g; brand mirrors disagreed 80/90/100 cal per oz so USDA basis per Butter-row precedent). Exact scale 9.33 oz, quantized 9.25 oz = 262 g (-0.9%). densities has no full-fat Cream Cheese row (FLAGGED); USDA tbsp = 14.5 g.

exact scale 1.56 cups, quantized 1.5 cups (-3.6%) = 357 g at densities 238 g/cup. Board 7 of 7. Standing shakedown observation about the Aldi dairy-free row no longer appears; today's Aldi cell is real heavy whipping cream.

ingredients.buy: 4.75 cups shredded, divided (half in, half on top)
ingredients.notes: existing ingredient-map entry (item Cheddar Cheese, Shredded -> cheddar-cheese-shredded, board weekly). Exact scale 4.67 cups, quantized 4.75 (+1.8%) = 537 g at densities 113 g/cup. BOARD DEFECTS OBSERVED, see board_defects_observed: the term-level weekly resolution goes to the generic shredded-cheese commodity whose Walmart cell is a Kraft Mac and Cheese boxed dinner, and the cheddar-cheese-shredded recipe-board id carries part-skim MOZZARELLA cells at Sam's/Family Fare/Hy-Vee. Not this recipe's call to fix; coverage is real either way.

dry mix, NOT the ranch-dressing (bottled) commodity - form flip. Exact scale 4.67 tsp = 1.56 tbsp, quantized 1.5 tbsp (-3.6%) = 10.5 g at densities 7 g/tbsp, rounded 11. FLAG: densities says 7 g/tbsp, the food-DB row says ~9 g/tbsp (MED conf); macro impact is under 3 cal/serving so not chased here, but the pair disagrees and the DB row's own note asks for packet verification. Board 6 of 7.

item_id NULL with reason: price-ingredient resolves 'bacon bits' to the raw bacon commodity via include /\bbacon\b/, but commodities.json's own bacon rule EXCLUDES 'bits', and the price class is wrong by roughly 3x (raw bacon $3.78-4.99/lb vs real capture evidence of bits at Hy-Vee $2.59/3.25 oz = ~$12.75/lb; bits are pre-cooked, concentrated product). Same rejection class as corn-chips-are-not-tortilla-chips. Null = pantry-static pricing, safe. Term ENQUEUED blocking for the pricer; carriage is the pricer's ruling, not made here (captures merely suggest it exists). Exact scale 1.17 cups = 18.7 tbsp, quantized 19 tbsp = 1 cup plus 3 tbsp (+1.8%) = 133 g at the Hormel label's 7 g/tbsp. NEW food-DB row added (Hormel Real Bacon Bits label).

pricing_terms_needed.why: board's only answer maps bits to raw bacon, a rejected price-class stretch; needs a real carriage/price verdict

new_commodity_proposals.registrar_ruling: NOT YET OBTAINED - the map lane cannot invoke the commodity-registrar agent; per plan S4 the ingredient maps item_id=null meanwhile (pantry-static, safe) and this proposal is a flagged follow-up for the registrar + capture pipeline. Evidence for the proposal: bacon commodity explicitly excludes 'bits'; capture evidence exists at 2+ stores (Hy-Vee ad 'bacon bits, 3.25 oz., $2.59' recurring through 2026-08-02; Walmart capture 'Oscar Mayer Real Bacon Bits, 3 oz Bag'); price class ~3-4x raw bacon per lb so it cannot share the bacon id.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS - protein gap 13.0% is inside the 15% tolerance, so portions stand. The main protein line is anchored by an explicit source WEIGHT (8 oz cooked), not an each-count, so the florentine failure mode does not apply. Gap direction is explained by (a) quantize-down on chicken and cream (-3.6% each) and (b) the source calculator's heavier cup-equivalents: its own '8 oz = about 2 cups' implies 113 g/cup where a nutrition calculator typically books shredded cheddar at 1 cup = 8 oz wt (227 g vs the label-accurate 113 g/cup used here), which alone would add roughly +75 cal and +6 g protein per serving to their figure.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 503 cal in [400, 650] PASS; carbs 8.2 g <= 35 PASS

term resolver ignores commodity excludes: 'bacon bits' resolves MAPPED to the bacon commodity by include /\bbacon\b/ even though the bacon rule's own exclude list contains 'bits' - any bits-like term will silently price as raw bacon
